narrative.overview: Sprint's interface is a stadium after dark: a near-black green-tinted ground, one volt-lime light carrying the page, and lane-line hairlines marking structure. The design shows machinery rather than decorating around it — boards move, queues retry, connectors draw.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated accent (volt) is allowed to carry whole regions; everything else stays quiet and dark.
Monospace is reserved for measurements, file names, and spec names — never as a "technical" costume.
Motion is calm but alive: the hero's WebGL ocean is the single authored moment; everything else reveals once and settles.
Honesty is visual too: sample data is labeled, claims are real, no invented proof.

rules.rule: The One-Light Rule. Volt is the only saturated color on the page. If a second hue must appear (amber retry states in illustrative data), it is semantic and temporary, never decorative.

dos: Keep secondary text tinted from the green hue (ink-secondary)
Use mono for measurements and spec names
